title: Region-aware retry signature and hedging SDK contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Different services and SDKs use divergent retry behaviors and idempotency semantics, causing data duplication and inconsistent failover results during multi-region outages and hedged calls. We have several follow-ups around backoff parameters but no unified mechanism for long-running/streaming requests or for hedged requests that may race across regions.

Goal: Define and ship a region-aware retry contract that introduces a stable request signature (idempotency signature) for non-trivial request shapes (including streaming/long-poll) and standard SDK knobs for hedged fanouts, circuit-breaker signals, and TTL-aware retries. The contract should be safe for common Redwood workloads: generation, embeddings, and reranking, and must play well with circuit breaker state and load-shedding decisions at the gateway and runtime layers.

Non-goals: Replacing existing per-service idempotency tokens today; this ticket specifies the contract, SDK changes, runtime adapters, and an incremental migration path.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/Go/TS) expose a single unified API for idempotency: request_signature and request_ttl with clear defaults
Runtime accepts request_signature hash and uses it for de-duplication across regions when within TTL
Hedging API supports explicit hedged=true plus max_fanout and hedge_delay_ms with sensible defaults documented
Circuit breaker state is propagated to clients via headers and SDKs adjust retry/backoff honoring circuit state and failover_policy
Telemetry emitted for retry_attempt, final_outcome, hedge_origin, idempotency_hash, and failover_region
No increase in customer-visible duplicate responses in staged rollout (validated by synthetic and real traffic tests)
Playbook updated with steps to handle stuck hedged requests and to inspect idempotency de-duplication keys
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with runtime, SDK, and console teams. Agreed on primary goals and non-goals.
2026-03-04: Drafted idempotency signature format — canonical JSON of (route, user_supplied_id, body_hash, content_type, streaming_marker) then SHA256 hex. Shared in #resilience.
2026-03-06: Prototype SDK patch (Python) for request_signature calculation. Stored logic in sdk/common/signature.py and validated on unit tests for sync/generator endpoints.
2026-03-09: Runtime adapter design completed: accept X-Req-Signature and X-Req-TTL headers, de-dupe store with 1-minute moving window for streaming preflight checkpoints.
2026-03-11: Integration test harness started that replays simulated failovers between us-east and eu-west and measures duplicate counts and latency.
2026-03-12: Discovered a race where hedged requests with very short hedge_delay_ms return both success tokens; added plan for single-response commit via de-dup key server-side commit
decisions: Use a deterministic request signature (not opaque client token) to enable cross-region de-duplication without global coordination.
Support idempotency for streaming by emitting periodic 'stream-checkpoint' markers that include the current signature and a monotonic sequence number.
Default hedge_delay_ms = 40ms and max_fanout = 2 for safety; SDKs can opt up for specific routes with per-route override in console.
Circuit breaker signals will be exposed via X-CB-State header with values (closed, open, degraded) and SDKs will switch to conservative backoff when open.
Backoff defaults are: first_retry_delay=150ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=2s for interactive routes; longer for batch/embeddings.
Security review required for signature format because it touches PII in some request bodies—default masks applied to known sensitive fields.
Rollout will be staged behind a feature flag per-customer with telemetry gating to detect increased duplications or latency regressions.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (SDKs): Add request_signature helper to Python/Go/TS. Expose high-level API: send(request, idempotency_hint=null, request_ttl_ms=60000, hedging_options=null).
Phase 2 (Runtime): Accept X-Req-Signature/X-Req-TTL, implement de-dup cache keyed by signature with TTL and commit semantics. Add single-response commit token to avoid double-success window.
Phase 3 (Gateway): Propagate X-CB-State and failover_region header; add failover_policy config mapping to per-route behavior.
Phase 4 (Observability): Instrument telemetry and dashboards; add alert if duplicate_ratio > 0.1% or hedged_latency_increase > 5%.
Phase 5 (Staged Rollout): Enable for internal services, then PLG customers opt-in, then gradual global rollout once metrics pass.
rollout_plan: Canary: Internal-only traffic with feature flag for 48 hours (us-east primary, eu-west fallback).
Beta: Selected customers (5) with heavy multi-region traffic for 2 weeks, daily review meetings.
Gradual: Increase to 25% traffic over 1 week, then 50% if telemetry stable, then full rollout.
Rollback: Toggle feature flag off; runtime will treat missing headers as legacy mode and fall back to existing per-service idempotency tokens.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signature canonicalization across languages (canonical JSON, stable field ordering, masking).
Property tests for streaming checkpoints ensuring monotonic checkpoint IDs and non-decreasing sequences.
Chaos tests that simulate region partition and validate de-duplication correctness and single-response commit behavior.
Load tests to validate de-dup cache performance at 10k req/s per region with 10s TTL.
Integration test with SDK hedging enabled and circuit breaker open to verify backoff adjustments.
notes: Next step: schedule security review and finalize masking rules for request canonicalization. Also sync with privacy team to ensure opt-in telemetry complies with customer agreements.
